=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: .github/workflows/plan.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 1140-1147 (perl -0pe fence stripper)
  Problem: The fence-stripper regex only removes fully closed fenced blocks. An unterminated fence opening marker (e.g., ` ```python\n...` with no closing ````) remains in CODEX_OUTPUT_PARSE_FILE verbatim. The downstream BLOCKED_REASON / clarification / self-check scanners will still correctly see content after the unterminated fence because the old `$in_code` toggle was removed — this is correct behavior.
  Why it fails at runtime: The comment on line 1150-1152 says "malformed/unclosed fences cannot hide a real BLOCKED line" — this claim is accurate for the BLOCKED_REASON scanner since it reads LINE-BY-LINE without any fence state. The concern raised by cross-pollination about unclosed fences leaving content behind is irrelevant because there is no longer any $in_code toggle in any scanner reading this file. All scanners (BLOCKED_REASON, SELF_CHECK counts, clarification grep, structured clarification block, auto-answer parser) now read CODEX_OUTPUT_PARSE_FILE or CODEX_OUTPUT_PARSE_FILE without any fence-state machine. The regex strip is a best-effort cleanup; even if it does nothing, removing the $in_code toggle from all consumers means the raw file content is always visible line-by-line.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: scripts/render_prompt.py
  Line or code reference: Lines 181-284 (_load_reference_placeholder_value + hydrate_reference_placeholders)
  Problem: The large refactor from the old dict-based REFERENCE_PLACEHOLDER_FILES/MODE_REFERENCE_APPEND_FILES to dynamic `_reference_file_name_for_placeholder` + `hydrate_reference_placeholders` changes behavior for ALL reference placeholders across every prompt mode, not just the three new Phase C references.
  Why it fails at runtime: The old `_reference_file_names_for_placeholder` raised `PromptLoadError("Unknown reference placeholder ...")` for unmapped placeholders. The new `_reference_file_name_for_placeholder` returns `None` for non-REFERENCE_ prefixed names but raises `PromptLoadError(f"Unsupported reference placeholder '{placeholder_name}'")` when the stem conversion produces an empty string or when a reference file is not found. This is a behavior change on error message wording and on the placeholder-allow-list: previously, a new `REFERENCE_SOMETHING` placeholder in a prompt would fail if not explicitly registered in the dict. Now, any `REFERENCE_XXX` placeholder will attempt to resolve `prompts/references/xxx.txt` dynamically via `discover_reference_path`. A typo in a placeholder name (e.g., `REFERENCE_OUTPUT_CONRTRACT`) now silently tries to load `prompts/references/output-conrtract.txt` and fails with a "not found" error, whereas before it would have failed with "Unknown reference placeholder". The behavioral difference is minor — both paths fail — but it weakens the allow-list property: *any* typo-suffix now becomes a file-not-found rather than a configuration-bug signal.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: .github/workflows/plan.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 1179-1200
  Problem: The perl sanitize command has no explicit error check between its execution and the downstream scans.
  Why it fails at runtime: If `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE` does not exist, perl -0pe creates an empty `CODEX_OUTPUT_PARSE_FILE` and exits 0. All downstream scanners (BLOCKED_REASON, SELF_CHECK counts, HAS_STATUS_NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, HAS_STRUCTURED_CLARIFICATION_BLOCK, auto-answer parser) would then read an empty file and uniformly conclude: no blocker, no self-check, no clarification. The workflow would proceed to approval as if Codex produced a clean plan, even though the input file was missing entirely.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
